scenario: ext4 mount at /srv/journal whose super options carry usrjquota=aquota.user and jqfmt=vfsv0 (journal quota): under the pre-seal amendment the ext quota-option vocabulary proves only that quota options are present, so quota_state is unknown / enforcement n/a / basis ext_quota_option_unverified, and the quota file name in the option value must never be echoed.

rationale: Superseded by the round-23 pre-seal amendment (preseal-amendment.md, section 'C2 final rules superseding only erroneous/ambiguous original clauses'); the original proposal in cases-proposed/CaseExt4Journaled.json remains an unaltered proposal and is not the sealed case. Derivation from contract.md (frozen at lane commit 4dc80c1be48308075e83af17f15fbfe7e95e6cb8) as corrected by that amendment, plus the named kernel sources only; no implementation was read (neither .ufo/waves/round-23/build/ImplQuota/ nor .scratch/round23/ImplQuota) and no test was run. (1) Mount resolution: probed path /srv/journal/data, realpath /srv/journal/data. The amendment keeps the longest component-prefix selection, so the candidates are the root line '/' and the ext4 line '/srv/journal', and the longest mount point wins: '/srv/journal', fstype 'ext4', mountinfo major:minor '8:2'. The amendment's new refusal rule (any covering mountpoint occurring more than once -> unknown/ambiguous_overmount) does not fire: '/' occurs once and '/srv/journal' occurs once in this mountinfo. Field layout per proc.rst section 3.5 (S082): six fixed fields, optional fields until the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and super options as the last field (proc.rst:1970-1983; 'Parsers should ignore all unrecognised optional fields', proc.rst:1985); the ext4 line carries the optional field 'shared:7' and no octal escapes, so root/mountpoint/source decode unchanged. Super options (last field) are 'rw,user_xattr,acl,jqfmt=vfsv0,usrjquota=aquota.user'. (2) Device check: fstype is ext4 (not btrfs) and the mountinfo major:minor '8:2' equals the path's st_dev '8:2', so the mismatch preemption (unknown/n/a/device_mismatch, device_check mismatch) does not fire; the btrfs stat-major-zero exemption is irrelevant to an ext4 mount (proc.rst:1975 defines field (3) as the 'value of st_dev for files on filesystem', S082). (3) Classification: the amendment states that for ext2/3/4 the quota_state is ALWAYS unknown with enforcement 'n/a', because mount option hints and journal-replay settings do not prove runtime accounting is enabled and S083 says the plain quota flags are ignored by the filesystem. The amendment also extends the ext quota-related vocabulary with 'noquota' and 'jqfmt' on top of the original keys (quota, usrquota, grpquota, prjquota, usrjquota, grpjquota). The chosen mount's super options contain two quota-related keys, 'usrjquota' and 'jqfmt', so the basis is 'ext_quota_option_unverified' rather than 'ext_quota_superblock_unobservable' (which is retained only when no quota-related key is present). Anchors: ext4.rst:261-265 'These options are ignored by the filesystem. They are used only by quota tools to recognize volumes where quota should be turned on.' and ext4.rst:267-271 'jqfmt=<quota type>, usrjquota=<file>, grpjquota=<file>' (S083); contract.md:118-119 for the original ext rows now superseded. (4) Verdict precedence: the single probed path is unknown and none is enabled, so exit 2 with finding_id QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN; QUOTA_ENABLED is a runway-reporting finding and would have applied under the original rows, which the amendment removes for ext4 because option presence is not proof of runtime accounting. (5) Fixture conformance to the amendment's new rules: btrfs_sysfs record 1d02a454-c549-4a35-b567-89d60902af8e carries the newly required member qgroups_enabled with the mandated pairing (qgroups false -> qgroups_enabled null, qgroups_mode null); the record has exactly the keys devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode. The uuid key is a canonical UUID, 'dm-0' is a plain basename, the single path is unique, normalized and absolute with no dot or dotdot components, and st_dev '8:2' is a canonical decimal MAJ:MIN. The btrfs uuid record is inert for this case (the chosen mount is ext4) but keeps the fixture a realistic host view with exactly the mandated top-level keys. (6) File-name non-disclosure: 'usrjquota=aquota.user' carries a quota file name in the option value (ext4.rst:267, S083); the contract requires option keys only and never file names from option values (contract.md:124-130) and the amendment repeats that quota option VALUES are never emitted. The scored per-path tuple carries only the six contract fields, so this property is not asserted by the tuple itself; it is recorded here and in the seat report as a supplementary-check gap (the amendment's 'supplementary sealed checks' clause mentions verifying quota_option_keys where given, but the six-field expected tuple has no slot for it).
